rationale: Narrow two of the snapshot question's remaining variants by source and correct one earlier counter-argument, without another execution. The correction: the StopSign adjustment of the equal case does not protect in the observed state, because it maps a request equal to the drifted decided index to the decided log without the StopSign (8) which is still above the content (6). The narrowings: the bound is computed on the node that receives the call, so a follower with the same drifted decided index would accept the same request, and local_only only controls forwarding; the form of the loss is whatever the entry type's Snapshot::create does with an empty slice. The account keeps its violated/asserted judgment on the same receipt.

interpretations.rationale: Witnessed, and the variants named in this question's discriminator are now narrowed by source with one earlier counter-argument corrected. Witness: with the drift in place (accepted 9, 9 and 6, decided 9, content six indices), snapshot(Some(8), false) returned Ok, the leader's compacted index became 8, and the snapshot reachable at index 0 held zero entry ids where the log had five decided entries (e70b8baa087246c78ea3a64f24b8e97c events 0-5); the comparisons requiring the compacted index to reach six and the snapshot to hold five entries were violated at the call event. Correction of an earlier counter-argument: I had written that the StopSign adjustment of the equal case might keep ordinary requests inside the entries; measured against the observed state it does not - a request equal to the drifted decided index would be mapped to the decided log without the StopSign, which is 8 rather than 9, and 8 still exceeds the content 6, so the equal case is not a protection here. Follower-side variant: the bound is computed from the decided index of the node that receives the call, so a follower whose own decided index has drifted the same way would accept the same request, with local_only only deciding whether the compaction is forwarded to the peers. Entry-type dependence: the loss takes the form the entry type's Snapshot::create gives to an empty slice; here that is an empty snapshot, and the reads then report a snapshotted region whose payload holds nothing.
counterevidence: The call itself returned Ok, so nothing in its result signals the loss; the witness is the compacted index together with the number of entries the produced snapshot holds.
The user supplied the index 8; the documented note allows any index up to the decided index, which was 9, so the request was inside the documented allowance rather than a caller error.
The apparent protection offered by the equal case does not hold in the observed state: it lowers the bound from 9 to 8, which is still above the content (6).
limitations: The consequence depends on the entry type's snapshot: here the snapshot records its input entries and is empty for an empty slice; an entry type that reconstructs state differently could behave differently.

The snapshot was requested with local_only false, so peers receive the forwarded compaction; their own compactions were sampled only through their accepted and decided indexes (events 4 and 5), not through their snapshots.

One three-node configuration, three reconnection rounds, one index and one entry type were exercised; the follower-side variant and the equal-index variant are argued from the derivation, not executed.

The comparisons that would tie the before and after samples to their admissions are unknown because of a shared event name in the same execution; the states are asserted from the sampled operands (events 0-5).
interpretations.joint_history: Same harness lineage as the drift account: receipt e70b8baa087246c78ea3a64f24b8e97c ran experiment a9cad483efbe4868a0d1c52a13253499-experiment, whose snap case reproduces receipt fd0b8be59c8f466fbf7768abb08f93b5 and whose new case uses the same snapshot-capable entry type and the same three reconnection rounds as the trim receipt ec3329dc273e452aa92bcd44652c116a; each case is read on its own samples and no measurement is combined across executions.
